title: Agentic Postgres provider bootstrap state
description: The record of which external provider resources this project owns. Root-owned, mode 0600, atomically replaced, one file per project under /etc/agentic-postgres/projects/{project_key}/. It records provider identifiers and file paths; it records no secret value and no client secret. Destruction and repair act on the IDs recorded here, never on a name lookup -- name equality is not ownership. See docs/decisions/0011-provider-bootstrap-state.md.

project_manifest_sha256.description: The whole manifest, for evidence. Deliberately NOT the convergence key: a domain or application change would otherwise force provider churn for resources that did not change.

provider_inputs_sha256.description: Computed only from provider-relevant non-secret inputs. This is the convergence key: a repeated --plan reports no changes when it matches.

runtime_client_id.description: The Universal Auth client ID. Non-secret by design -- it is a username. The matching client secret is never in this file; it lives only in the root-owned 0400 file named by credential_files.client_secret_path.

active_client_secret_id.description: The provider's identifier FOR the secret, not the secret. Rotation revokes by this ID after a replacement has been written and validated, so a failed rotation can never leave the project with no working credential.

credential_files.description: Paths, not contents. Both are under the per-project credential directory, so the path itself carries the project scope and a state file naming another project's directory is detectable. The `_path` suffix is load-bearing, not decoration: a key literally named `client_secret` is rejected by the inherited sensitive-key rule (ADR 0008), and correctly so -- the rule cannot tell that this one holds a filename. Naming the field for what it contains satisfies the rule without weakening it.

managed_resources.description: What this project created and is therefore allowed to destroy. An enum rather than free text: destruction reads this list, and a typo that silently widened it would be the worst possible bug in this file. A secret entry is the contract's own `name` from secrets.required.yaml, one per secret; test_bootstrap_state.py asserts this enum covers every required secret that file declares, because bootstrap creating one credential while materialization expected three is exactly the drift that produced a 404 in the middle of a deployment.

providerId.description: A provider resource identifier. Mandatory before a resource is treated as managed: without an ID, destruction would have to fall back to a name lookup, and a name is not proof of ownership.
